newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH NMB-HELLER SEES PROFIT GAIN.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH NMB-HELLER SEES PROFIT GAIN.

text.p: NMB-Heller Holding NV, a 50-50 joint venture of Fuji Bank unit Heller International and ING , said 1996 profits would rise by around 10 percent.
"Profits are likely to increase by about 10 percent," director Hans Groenen said in a telephone interview.
In 1995 profits rose 23.5 percent to 50.1 million guilders on 26.3 percent higher turnover of 16.5 billion guilders.
Earlier the Dutch factoring and corporate financing company said it agreed to buy Britain's biggest independent factoring firm TI-Heller, which is now called ING-Heller Ltd.
The director said margins were slightly under pressure.
He added NMB-Heller's business growth in France had been slowed down as there had been a lot of bankruptcies there.
"We have downgraded our growth strategy in France," he said.
Groenen added it was not actively seeking more acquisitions in Europe, but did not rule out such a step in the future.
"It is easier to grow through acquisitions than by starting your own business in another country," he said.
NMB-Heller currently operates in the Netherlands, Germany, Britain and France and has joint ventures in Poland and the Czech Republic.
